claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies and limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Hot forging at approximately 900 °C followed by a short anneal at approximately 800 °C will refine the dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will reduce interlamellar spacing and refine boundary structures.
The treated alloy will contain refined lamellar boundaries and reduced interlamellar spacing.
Refining the lamellar structure shortens the dislocation mean free path.
Refining the lamellar structure disperses dislocation pile-ups.
Dispersing dislocation pile-ups reduces local stress concentrations at phase interfaces.
Reducing interfacial stress concentrations lowers the driving force for microcrack nucleation and delays catastrophic failure.
Internal-stress accumulation and strain localization near lamellar phase boundaries promote crack propagation and coalescence along interfaces.
The untreated alloy has coarse lamellae that cause early dislocation pile-up.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile ductility by at least 20% relative to the as-cast material.
The treatment will maintain or slightly improve yield strength relative to the as-cast material.
Grain or microstructural refinement through thermomechanical processing can enhance strength while retaining useful ductility in high-entropy alloys.
The predicted response applies to room-temperature tensile testing at approximately 10^-3 s^-1 under ordinary laboratory conditions.
Processing conditions that coarsen the lamellae or severely change phase fractions will diminish or eliminate the strength and ductility benefits.
The magnitude of improvement depends on forging time, temperature, strain rate, deformation level, and alloy chemistry.
Failure to obtain at least 20% higher ductility while maintaining or improving yield strength under identical testing conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
Persistence of early microcracks at lamellar boundaries after treatment would falsify the proposed mechanism.
